summary: SARhythm is an instrument-grade radar water-loss monitor built for government water agencies and parametric insurers. Using 12-day L-band radar observations from the NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite, SARhythm tracked Lake Tisza's Tiszavalki Basin during Hungary's severe 2026 drought—measuring −6.98 km² (−15.9%) of open-water contraction as the reservoir dropped 140 cm (749 cm to 609 cm). Unlike optical satellites that were 66.6% blocked by clouds at peak water stage and missed ~24% of flooded area beneath floating water-chestnut mats, L-band radar penetrated both cloud cover and wetland foliage, matching cloud-free NASA OPERA optical water loss (−6.94 km²) within 0.04 km² while grading every sector with transparent confidence checks.
details:
What It Does: SARhythm transforms multi-temporal satellite radar into a plain-language drought risk map, a ranked list of severely drying basin sectors, and an auditable physical evidence ledger. Decision-makers can immediately identify critical drying zones (such as Sector 05, which lost 89.3 ha or 56% of its June water extent), step through all 11 satellite overpasses across the 2026 season, and expand an on-demand verification drawer to inspect signal-to-noise checks, radar scattering physics, and cross-sensor validation.

How It Works:

  1. Single-Orbit Processing Consistency: Queries 11 ascending passes of NISAR L2-GCOV (Track 057 / Frame 026, 20 m × 20 m, EPSG:32634), isolating the 10-epoch Provisional series (CRID P05023, Jun 18–Oct 16) from the Validated observation (CRID P05036, Oct 28; +0.15 dB urban offset verified).
  2. Scene-Adaptive Classification & 4-Class Mask Differencing: Derives a water threshold independently per date from permanent pelagial deep-water reference blocks and each scene's bimodal histogram valley (−14.53 to −15.07 dB), then differences binary masks into Persistent Water, Likely Water Loss, Likely Water Gain, and Land/Reed Margin.
  3. Habitat-Aware Physics & Statistical Guard Band: Stratifies open water from emergent Phragmites reedbeds using baseline cross-polarized (HV) backscatter—capturing opposite physical drying signatures (+1.66 dB brightening as open water exposes rough mud in Sector 19 vs. −1.48 dB darkening as standing water vanishes beneath reed stems in Sector 04). Every measurement is tested against a guard band of $T_{\text{final}} = \pm 5.33\text{ dB}$ (computed numerically from the two-sided $\alpha = 0.01$ $F$-distribution at $L = 9.6$ effective looks, bounded against $3\hat{\sigma}_{\text{MAD}}$ across 20 urban and 12 deep-water reference polygons) and scored across 4 explicit Pass/Warn confidence gates.
  4. Transparent Outage & Regulation Handling: Explicitly flags comparisons spanning NISAR's July 27–August 10 instrument outage and incorporates KÖTIVIZIG's October 22, 2026 water-retention order ("Vízvisszatartás a Tisza-tóban") so October water retention is never confused with scheduled winter draining.

Tools & Stack: Python 3.14 (earthaccess, h5py, numpy, scipy, rasterio, pandas, Pillow) for offline HDF5 byte-range streaming and metrology; zero-dependency HTML5/CSS3/Vanilla JS/SVG static frontend for instantaneous, 100% offline field deployment.
